title: Add Support for EIP-7939 (CLZ Opcode) in the FEVM
description: Introduces the CLZ (Count Leading Zeros) opcode (0x1e) to the FEVM, matching Ethereum's EIP-7939 behavior. CLZ provides a fast, gas-efficient way to count leading zero bits in a 256-bit word, widely used in math operations, compression, bitmap navigation, and ZK proving workflows.

storageProviders: No direct impact on storage providers. The CLZ opcode operates at the FEVM smart contract execution layer and does not affect sector management, proof-of-power, or block production.
clients: No direct impact on clients, but they can indirectly benefit from lower execution costs and improved developer experience for FEVM applications that rely on efficient bit-level operations.
tokenHolders: No change to Filecoin consensus incentives or token economics. By reducing on-chain computation costs for certain workloads, the opcode may enable new application patterns.
applicationDevelopers: Developers can use the native CLZ opcode instead of multiple shifts, comparisons, and constants in Solidity — significantly saving gas and bytecode size.
CLZ(0) returns 256, a design choice that is convenient for byte/word scanning patterns and enables compact downstream computations (e.g., CLZ(0) >> 3 == 32).
Particularly beneficial for ZK proving systems: dynamic shifts are disproportionately expensive in zero-knowledge proofs, and native CLZ substantially reduces proving overhead.
Backwards compatibility note: before activation, opcode 0x1e is an undefined instruction causing execution abort; after activation it will execute CLZ semantics.
